newsitem.title: USA: Cyprus promised no Greek warplanes for 13 months.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus promised no Greek warplanes for 13 months.

text.p: Cyprus has assured the United States that no Greek warplanes will be deployed for the next 13 months to a new airbase under construction on the Mediterranean island, the State Department said on Monday.

"I believe ... that the assurance that we have is that Greek military aircraft will not be deployed to the new base on Cyprus for 13 months," spokesman Nicholas Burns said, confirming a Washington Post story published on Sunday.
The term of office of Cyprus President Glafcos Clerides will end in 13 months' time.

Burns told a news conference that Cyprus made the promise to U.S. diplomat Carey Cavanaugh during a mission he made to the divided island last month in an effort to defuse tensions and promote prospects for a settlement.

The United States had already publicised a promise that Clerides made to Cavanaugh to wait at least 16 months before receiving any components of an anti-aircraft missile system that Cyprus plans to buy from Russia.
News of the purchase prompted Turkish officials to threaten military strikes to prevent deployment of the system.

Cyprus has been divided betwen Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities since mainland Turkish troops invaded the northern third of the island in 1974 following a Greek Cypriot military coup in Nicosia. Repeated diplomatic efforts to reunite the island have failed.
Under a 1993 defence pact with Greece, Cyprus is building a military airfield at Paphos that could accommodate Greek F-16 warplanes in case of a renewed crisis.
New U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said at Senate confirmation hearings last month that tackling the Cyprus problem would be one of her priorities.
